# Applying a foundation

A foundational idea becomes useful when a learner can recognize how it applies in a new example. Start by identifying the relevant parts of the example, then connect those parts to the idea. Explain the connection in your own words and check whether the explanation accounts for the important details.

When an example looks different from earlier practice, compare its structure rather than its surface appearance. Notice which details matter, which details are incidental, and what would change if one condition were different. This process supports transfer without assuming that every new case is identical to a familiar one.

Use the worked example, pause to predict the result, and then compare the prediction with the explanation. A useful answer names the idea, applies it to the evidence in the example, and gives a reason for the conclusion.
